properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf expected.

* WHERE...Beaches of Volusia, Indian River, Saint Lucie, Martin,
and Brevard Counties.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

potential for falling and/or blowing snow with strong winds and

properties.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued November 15 at 11:40AM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Winter Weather Advisory above 6000 feet, moderate
snow expected. Total snow accumulations 2 to 8 inches, with up to
16 inches near Lassen Volcanic National Park. Winds gusting as high
as 40 mph. For the Winter Storm Watch above 4000 feet, heavy snow
possible. Total snow accumulations between 1 and 2 feet above 5000
feet possible, with up to 3 feet at the highest peaks. Total snow
accumulations of 4 to 8 inches between 4000 feet to 5000 feet, with
up to 12 inches at 5000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 50 mph.

* WHERE...For the Winter Weather Advisory, Northern Sierra above 6000
feet, including Highway 50, Interstate 80, State Route 4, State
Route 108, Southern Cascades above 6000 feet, including Lassen
National Park. For the Winter Storm Watch, elevations above 4000
feet in the Sierra Nevada and southern Cascades.

* WHEN...For the Winter Weather Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to
10 PM PST Monday. For the Winter Storm Watch, from Tuesday evening
through early Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Snow covered roads, travel delays, and chain controls
possible this afternoon into Monday. The hazardous conditions will
impact the Monday morning and evening commutes. Travel could be
very difficult to impossible Tuesday night through early Friday
morning. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches and significant
reductions in visibilities.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels 6500 to 7500 feet today, dropping
to around 5000 to 6000 feet Monday. Heaviest snow is expected late
tonight into Monday morning. Lull in activity expected on Tuesday,
followed by a colder, stronger system by mid-week. Snow levels
3500-4500 feet Tuesday night, rising to around 4500-6000 feet
Wednesday. Heaviest snow is expected Wednesday afternoon into the
overnight hours, with snowfall rates 1-2+ inches per hour.
properties.instruction:
Check the latest road conditions from Caltrans online at
quickmap.dot.ca.gov or dial 5 1 1.
